items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 43:1
items.html: (to question) The expansion and departure that were in Partzuf Keter of AK are called Yod-Hey. The second expansion and second departure that were in Partzuf AB of AK are called Vav-Hey. The Yod-Hey in the first expansion are also incorporated in the second expansion since all the forces in the upper one are necessarily present in the lower one, as well. You find that Yod-Hey is in Keter, meaning in Partzuf Keter of AK, and HaVaYaH in the rest of the Partzufim. (page 309, item 23, and in Inner Light, page 310, the passage beginning “And this is what he says”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 44:1
items.html: (to question) The letters are in the secret of vessels. It is known that the departure of the light and its absence cause the making of the vessel. Hence it is necessary that in each of the four letters HaVaYaH there is some discernment of a lack of light. This is the cause for the making of that letter, meaning that vessel, and this is why the letters are lacks. (page 309, the passage beginning “Four deficiencies”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 45:1
items.html: (to question) The Yod implies the expansion of the light of Nekudot [dots] of Partzuf Keter, which are the levels that emerged there from Hochma and below. Vav implies the expansion light of Nekudot of Partzuf AB of AK, meaning from Hochma and below of this Partzuf, as well. However, there is no sign of the expansion of the level of Keter in the four letters HaVaYaH, neither of Keter of Partzuf Keter, nor of Keter of Partzuf AB, since there is no deficiency there, for which the letters would be written, as written in answer 44 above. (page 309, items 24 and 25)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 46:1
items.html: (to question) The First Hey implies the general departure of the first expansion, and the last Hey implies the general departure of the second expansion. (There, and in Inner Light)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 47:1
items.html: (to question) Because the whole matter of the vessels of reception, called Guf, are because of the reflected light that Malchut raises in her striking on the upper light from her and above in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh. Through this reflected light, Malchut acquires strength to expand from her and within her from above downward to ten Sefirot of clothing, called Guf. This means that the entire amount that the reflected light clothed in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh from below upward are themselves inverted and clothe ten Sefirot of the Guf. Thus, the ten Sefirot of the Guf are branches of the Malchut of the Rosh. (page 291, item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 48:1
items.html: (to question) It stands under Malchut of the Rosh, meaning under its root. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 49:1
items.html: (to question) It bestows upon its branch, which stands in the vessel of Keter of the Guf, which is the discernment of the male of Keter. It also prevents the illumination of GAR from expanding to the Partzuf. (page 324, the passage beginning “And there is”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 50:1
items.html: (to question) Because although the lights departed from the Guf, they still receive enough light to sustain them. They receive this illumination through the Keter that departed from them and rose under Malchut of the Rosh, since it is the root of every ten Sefirot of the Guf, as the light of Keter always contains all the ten Sefirot that expand through it. (page 292, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “Their faces”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 51:1
items.html: (to question) It indicates that it is a light without a vessel; hence, it cannot expand from above downward to the Guf. Its being under Malchut of the Rosh and above the vessels of the Guf indicates that it is a medium, an intermediate between the discernment of the Rosh and the discernment of the Guf, shining from its place to the Guf through its record that stands at the Keter of the Guf. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 52:1
items.html: (to question) It causes its branches in the Guf, which are ZON in the vessel of Keter that receive its illumination, not to be able to bestow that great light that they receive from it to the lower ones from Keter of the Guf. This is so because the posterior of the light of Keter detains and stops its illumination so as not to expand from the vessel of Keter of the Guf downward. (page 292, items 4 and 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 53:1
items.html: (to question) It is a sufficient illumination to descend below to clothe in the Guf to mate and generate offspring. (page 292, item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 54:1
items.html: (to question) Through two couplings that are induced in Malchut of the Rosh, ZON acquire the strength to descend to clothe in the Guf and generate offspring. (page 292, the passage beginning “The Keter”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 55:1
items.html: (to question) Through the ascents of the male of Keter, namely phase four of clothing, with the female of Keter, namely phase three in complete coarseness, both from extension and from clothing, these ZON participate in one another in a common coarseness. At that time, the male attains both from the discernment of extension, and these common MAN cause a discernment of upper coupling in Malchut of the Rosh, and the level that emerges of this coupling attains up to Keter of the Rosh. Also, the light of Keter in Malchut receives this great light and bestows it to its branches, which are ZON. This is considered that it turned its anterior back to its branches. (page 298, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And therefore she made”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 56:1
items.html: (to question) The ascents of ZON to the Rosh mean that the coarseness in them is refined and their form equalized with the discernment of Malchut of the Rosh. This causes the coupling in Malchut of the Rosh, which draws the light from the upper Keter, as written in answer 55 above. At that time, the light of Keter returns its anterior to the branches and bestows upon them the light of the upper Keter. However, after the second coupling, when ZON have already suckled enough to descend to the Guf for clothing in the vessels, the lights of ZON return and grow coarser in the coarseness of the Guf. At that time, they cause that the discernment of intermediate coarseness, mentioned in answer 51, that exists in the light of Keter, which is its posterior, which deny its illumination from the Guf since it lacks phase four of extension. For this reason, no vessel of reception is extended from the first coupling, and this absence of vessels of reception is itself its discernment of posterior to the branches. (page 300, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And then it needs”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 57:1
items.html: (to question) These changes and operations that the discernments of the Guf cause to be renewed in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh do not refer to the very essence of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, but only to the Malchut and the screen in it. This is according to the reflected light that she raises up from below upward. For this reason, Malchut is considered the root of all the vessels and the lights in them, and all the incidents in the ten Sefirot of the Guf. Hence, when her branches acquire equivalence of form with her, they instantly return to her, as a branch that returns to its root. Through this return, the branches are renewed and they cause the discernment of renewed coarseness in the screen in Malchut. The upper light, which does not stop for a moment, copulates on the new form of coarseness that the screen attained by the incorporation of the branches in it. At that time, a level of new ten Sefirot comes out there “in potential,” appearing from there to the Guf in practice. (page 295, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “They”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 58:1
items.html: (to question) The male of Keter of Keter is the record of the vessel of Keter of the first expansion that was renewed in the upper coupling of the Rosh. The female is the actual light of the level of Hochma that emerged through a coupling of the upper light on the coarseness of phase three from Malchut of the Rosh upward, which was inverted and descended to the Guf from Malchut downward. (page 297, item 9, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “That is refined”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 59:1
items.html: (to question) The refinement of the screen in Tabur of the first expansion until it became refined in equivalence of form to the screen of Malchut of the Rosh is considered that the screen of Tabur rose to the Rosh. As it ascends in the order of degrees of the ten Sefirot of the Guf, the screen is incorporated with all the records in the Guf. The two records of male and female of Keter are the upper ones among them, containing all of them. Hence, when that screen rose to the Rosh, it brought these records with it, meaning ZON of Keter. Thus, the refinement of the screen of the first expansion caused ZON of Keter to rise up to the Rosh. (page 293, the passage beginning “Ascend”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 60:1
items.html: (to question) It is after the two couplings of ZON were completed. In the first coupling, which was the incorporation of the female in the male, they extended the light from the upper Keter. However, they still did not have the strength to turn over and expand downward to the Guf. This is so because the coarseness of phase four of the male was lacking the discernment of extension of phase four since Malchut did not leave a record. That coarseness of phase four of clothing was sufficient to make a coupling of the Rosh by joining with the record of phase three. However, she was still not enough to make a vessel of reception for clothing in the Guf through that reflected light. Hence, the ZON could not descend to the Guf until a second coupling was done, where there was an incorporation of the male in the female, and the coupling came out on phase three, which has the discernment of extension, too. At that time, Malchut of the Rosh could expand from her and within her into ten Sefirot of the Guf to the Chazeh, and the ZON could come down. (page 293, the passage beginning “And afterward”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 61:1
items.html: (to question) The ascent of ZON upward caused the making of a coupling on phase three, which lowered only the level of Hochma to the Guf, and the light of Keter remained in the Rosh. Thus, the degrees descended because the light of Hochma clothed in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, etc. It therefore follows that each and every vessel remained lacking much of that measure of light that it had in the first expansion. For this reason, the coarseness in the vessels had been recognized, and they were completed in a way that they will not be canceled by the light that is clothed there. It follows that the ascents of ZON caused the completion of the vessels. (page 293, the passage beginning “It was necessary”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 62:1
items.html: (to question) It is because the highest Sefira contains all the Sefirot below it. Hence, the record of phase four contains all the records below her, but because she lacks the discernment of extension, she must therefore join with the phase three. Hence, phase three, too, merits a name, and they are all named after the two records, which are ZON of the vessel of Keter. (page 294, the passage beginning “And know that their essence”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 63:1
items.html: (to question) The record of phase four, which is the male of Keter, is only half a record, its weaker half, which is only the discernment of clothing. However, the record of phase three is complete with two discernments of coarseness: of clothing and of extension. The male becomes needy of the female, to the extent that there is equivalence between them, and they become ZON of a single degree. (page 294, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And know that these”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 64:1
items.html: (to question) Under the root light of Keter, which stands under Malchut of the Rosh, since the ZON are the branches of that light of Keter. (page 297, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And remember”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 65:1
items.html: (to question) The coming of phase three, which is the female of the vessel of Keter to the place of Malchut of the Rosh. It causes a corresponding ascent of Malchut of the Rosh to Yesod of the Rosh, which is phase three of the Rosh. (page 295, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “They”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 66:1
items.html: (to question) See Answers to the Meaning of the Words, answer 13.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 67:1
items.html: (to question) The first is the incorporation of the lights of ZON when they are without vessels, meaning when they ascend to the Rosh. At that time, they have both been refined and acquired the form of Malchut of the Rosh, which is not considered an actual vessel, where ZON are incorporated in one another in two couplings. The second is when they are in two vessels, and their illumination is incorporated in one another, which is in ZON of the vessel of Keter of Partzuf AB. The third is when both are clothed in one vessel, are incorporated in one another, and this is in Partzuf SAG of AK, when the female is clothed there in the male vessel of Keter. (page 357, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 68:1
items.html: (to question) The record of phase four is half a record from the coarseness of clothing, devoid of coarseness of extension. Hence, she is not suitable to draw any light, unless by joining with the record of the female, which is coarseness of phase three, which is complete with the discernment of extension, too. For this reason, these two records are regarded as two parts of a body, where one gives the clothing, and one gives the extension. This is why they are called ZON.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 69:1
items.html: (to question) The male is the light of Keter, and the female is the light of Hochma. (page 292, and in Inner Light 2, the passage beginning “The male”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 70:1
items.html: (to question) Each branch stands under its proximate root. The light of Keter stands under Malchut of the Rosh; the light of the male, which is a record of that light of Keter, stands below it, and the light of the female, which is the record of coarseness of phase three, considered a branch of phase four, stands under the male. (page 297, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And remember”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 71:1
items.html: (to question) They make two couplings: The first is on the coarseness that is made of phase four of clothing with phase three of extension. This coupling draws nearly the level of Keter. The second is a coupling made only on coarseness of phase three. This coupling draws only the level of Hochma. (page 299, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And then she is incorporated”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 72:1
items.html: (to question) ZON of the vessel of Keter that participate in their kinds of coarseness together, cause the ascent of Malchut to the Yesod of the Rosh, which is phase three of the Rosh. Also, they participate there together like ZON of Keter of the Guf. This is so because Malchut is phase four, and the Yesod is phase three. Thus, the light of Yesod did not rise up and Malchut was not refined from her phase four when she rose to the Yesod, but only to the extent of the lack of extension that the male of the vessel of Keter lacked. Hence, the coupling that emerged on the common coarseness of Yesod and Malchut of the Rosh drew nearly the level of Keter. The lights of the Rosh did not exchange their places, and the light of Keter remained in its place, and did not descend to the degree of Hochma. For this reason, the illumination of the upper Keter was elicited by that coupling. (page 299, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “However, you will see”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 73:1
items.html: (to question) When Malchut of the Rosh is not completely refined to phase three, but receives phase four of clothing of the male of the vessel of Keter inside her, she then participates with phase three of the Rosh. In this manner, she draws the light of the upper Keter, and the lights do not exchange their places, see answer 72 above. (page 299, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And for this reason”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 74:1
items.html: (to question) During the ascent of Malchut of the Rosh to Yesod of the Rosh only in the form of association, and not in the form of refinement, see answer 73 above. (page 294, item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 75:1
items.html: (to question) Phase three, which is the female, which has the discernment of extension, too, participates with phase four of the male and incorporates with him in one screen. At that time, nearly the level of Keter is drawn upon it. (page 299, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And then she is incorporated”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 76:1
items.html: (to question) Malchut of the Rosh ascends to Yesod from the discernment of refinement to phase three and an upper coupling in the level of Hochma emerges on the screen in her. At that time, the degrees descend there since the light of Hochma clothes in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, etc. It follows that Keter descended to the degree of Hochma, and Hochma descended to the degree of Bina, etc. This is so because the vessel is drawn primarily after the light in it. When the light of Hochma clothes the vessel of Keter, Keter descends to the degree of Hochma, etc. (page 300, item 10, and in Inner Light there, the passage beginning “The root”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 77:1
items.html: (to question) Because the discernment of extension from the coarseness of phase four is missing there. Because of that lack, Malchut cannot expand from her and within her to ten Sefirot of the Guf to Malchut of Malchut, called Tabur. (page 300, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And then it needs”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 78:1
items.html: (to question) When Keter’s time to go back down to the Guf from above downward comes, although it has not returned, still, the discernment of the Guf contained in it since it was in the first expansion has awakened. This is in disparity of form from the discernment of Malchut of the Rosh, and it is known that disparity of form separates and parts the spirituals. For this reason, it is considered to have gone out from Malchut of the Rosh. (page 300, item 10, and in Inner Light, page 301, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 79:1
items.html: (to question) The previous incorporation of the female in the male, which was in the first coupling, which equalized them together, caused the male to be incorporated later in the female in the second coupling. (page 301, item 11)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 80:1
items.html: (to question) Through these couplings, ZON are incorporated together. The male is incorporated in the new level of light of Hochma, all of which expands and descends to the Guf, and the female acquired illumination from upper Keter. In that, they unite and incorporate in the vessel of Keter of the Guf, as well, and both also receive from the posterior of the light of Keter. (page 324, the passage beginning “And we should understand”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 81:1
items.html: (to question) Through the ascent of the screen of Tabur of the first departure to the Rosh, it raised these two records of phase four and phase three with it. These are ZON of the vessel of Keter, where they were incorporated in Malchut of the Rosh in the two couplings, received their completion, and descended to the Guf to the vessel of Keter. (page 325, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And therefore”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 82:1
items.html: (to question) The Nukva left the posterior of the vessel of Keter because of the clash of surrounding light and inner light, and was also refined from phase three to phase two. At that time, the level of Bina emerged on phase two and gave to the vessel of Hochma. Also, the male of Keter, which is phase four, was refined into phase three, and gave this residue to the vessel of Hochma. He became the male of the vessel of Hochma, and the level of Bina that was emanated from the female became the discernment of female of the vessel of Hochma. (page 319, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 83:1
items.html: (to question) The male was emanated through the turning of the face of the vessel of Hochma to shine, a vessel of giving lights, meaning only the turning of the face from the discernment of GAR to the discernment of VAK. It was still not refined to phase one. At that time, ZON of the vessel of Hochma mated and engendered the male of Bina, which is Yod, from the discernment of VAK in them. They gave it to the vessel of Bina, where he became the discernment of male of Bina. Afterwards, the vessel of Hochma was refined into phase one, over which the level of light of Hesed emerged, and gave it to the vessel of Bina. This is considered a son of Bina, and the record in the vessel of Bina from the time of the first expansion became the discernment of female of Bina. (page 320, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “The Hochma”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 84:1
items.html: (to question) Two couplings: 1 – The incorporation of the female in the male and the level that is extended in the measure of the male. 2 – The incorporation of the male in the female and the level is extended in the measure of the female. (page 298, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And therefore”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 85:1
items.html: (to question) In ZON of Keter of AB of AK, the first coupling is nearly on the level of Keter, and the second coupling is in the level of Hochma. However, ZON of Keter of SAG, the first coupling is nearly in the level of Hochma, and the second coupling is in the level of Bina.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 86:1
items.html: (to question) In Hochma of AB, the male is on the level of Hochma, and the female is on the level of Bina. In ZON of Hochma of SAG of AB, the male is on the level of Bina, extended from the coupling of ZON of Keter, and the female is the discernment of the record of Bina in the vessel of Hochma from the time of the first expansion. (page 341, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 87:1
items.html: (to question) In ZON of Bina of AB, the male is the discernment of VAK of GAR, meaning VAK of Hochma, and the female is the discernment of the record of the first expansion. In ZON of Bina of SAG, they are discernments of records that remained from the second expansion, from the lights of ZON of Bina of AB after their departure. (page 342, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And the ZON”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 88:1
items.html: (to question) The five edges of AB contain illumination of Hochma, but the five edges of SAG contain only illumination of Bina. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 89:1
items.html: (to question) Two lights in the vessel of Hochma, which are ZON, and three lights in the vessel of Bina, which are the male and female of Bina, and the light of Hesed in Bina, containing the whole ZAT. (page 352, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “Ascents”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 90:1
items.html: (to question) When the screen is refined and there is no coupling in Keter, the name Yod-Hey is simple, without filling. When there is a coupling in Keter, the name Yod-Hey is in filling. (page 352, item 56)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 91:1
items.html: (to question) Four lights rise in AB of AK, and five lights rise in SAG of AK. (page 352, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “Sometimes”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 92:1
items.html: (to question) The Hey of Yod-Hey is filled with Yod like this: Hey-Yod. This is because the lower three of the four lights are canceled in the upper one in them, which is light of Hochma implied in the Yod. (page 353, item 56)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 93:1
items.html: (to question) The letters themselves are vessels, and their filling is the measure of the coarseness in the screen in them. The measure of the level is evaluated by them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 94:1
items.html: (to question) The measure of coarseness of phase three and phase two are Yods; the measures of coarseness of phase one is Alephs; and the discernments of light of Malchut are the Heys. (page 353, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “With Yods”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 95:1
items.html: (to question) When the letters are without a filling, it indicates that there is no coarseness in the screen in them, and there is no coupling by striking that draws light. (page 354, item 58)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 96:1
items.html: (to question) The male and female are equal to each other when they are without light, but are only as records. Although the male is a record of the Keter, and the female is a record of Hochma, which is much lower than Keter, still, because it is devoid of phase four of extension, because of which the light of Keter remains in the Rosh, and is not destined to return to the Partzuf, hence, his record is very small. However, the record of the female is complete in the discernment of extension, too, and her light, which is the light of Hochma, is destined to return to the Partzuf in its entirety. Thus, a great light still remains in her record until she equalizes with the record of the male, although she is from the discernment of Keter. Nevertheless, after they rise to the Rosh and are incorporated there in two couplings, where in the first coupling, the record of male received the illumination of upper Keter, then the male is much greater than the Nukva. Even though the female is incorporated with him, she can still receive only VAK from him, and not illumination of GAR. Thus, the female is considered the discernment of VAK with respect to the male. (page 354, item 59)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 97:1
items.html: (to question) ZON are in two vessels in the first discernment of the second expansion, called AB of AK. In the second discernment of the second expansion, called SAG of AK, ZON are in one vessel. (page 356, item 60)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 98:1
items.html: Because of the incorporation of the female in the male in the two

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 98:2
items.html: (to question) couplings of the Rosh, her measure of light grew extensively, and she needs a new vessel that will fit her measure of light. She acquires that vessel in Partzuf AB through the striking of the record and the light of Hochma against one another. Since there was no such striking in SAG, no sparks emerged for the vessel of the female; therefore, she must clothe in the vessel of the male. (page 354, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “On the occasion”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 99:1
items.html: (to question) In the second departure, when ZON rose to Malchut of the Rosh, ZON were incorporated there in two couplings, similar to the ascents of ZON after first departure. Here, too, the female received illumination of the upper Keter in the first coupling, but the difference is that here, the degrees descended and there was light of Hochma in the vessel of the upper Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 100:1
items.html: (to question) The light of Keter that remained in the Rosh and did not return to the Guf of AB, it turned to its branches and prevented illumination of GAR from them. Similarly, the light of Hochma that did not return to the Guf of Partzuf SAG of AK, turned its posterior to the branches, too, and prevented illumination of GAR from them. Thus, the female could receive from the light of the male only illumination of VAK. (page 356, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “There is no”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 101:1
items.html: (to question) Because in Partzuf SAG, the degrees and ZON of Keter here descended, similar to ZON of Hochma of AB. Also, ZON of Hochma here are similar to ZON of Bina in Partzuf AB. Hence, ZON of Hochma here contain only the discernment of VAK of Hochma, similar to the male of Bina of AB, and the female is only a record, similar to the female of Bina of AB, called Dalet. The male, which is VAK, is called Vav, since every VAK is called Vav and not Yod. Still, in themselves they are sometimes called Yod-Hey, like ZON of Bina of AB. (page 356, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “And from a coupling”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 102:1
items.html: (to question) It is a rule that there is only ascent of MAN to the female. Hence, when four lights rise to Keter, which are ZON of Hochma and ZON of Bina, and the light of Hesed remains in the Partzuf, which is in Partzuf AB of AK, where the light of Hesed remained before it completed all of its ten inlets. At that time, the lights rise in the vessel of the female of Keter, since there are two vessels to ZON. However, when five lights ascend to Keter, which is only in Partzuf SAG, as there is a perpetual expansion and departure there, and each time it expands to Malchut, all the lights ascend to Keter, and it expands in Keter once more. Thus, five lights ascend here, which are ZON of Hochma, ZON of Bina, and the light Hesed, which contain the entire ZAT. Here the lights rise to the vessel of the male of Keter, called Yod, because there is only one vessel to the ZON here. Thus, although they rise to the female, here the female itself is in the vessel of the male; hence, the lights rise after it to the vessel of the male. All this refers only to the ascent of the lights to Keter, but at the end of the departure, when they rise to the Rosh, all the lights incorporate in the ZON of Keter and annul in them since the upper lights are somewhat incorporated in the male, and somewhat in the female, like the two couplings that ZON make there. In the first coupling, when the female of Keter is incorporated in the male, all the lights follow her and incorporate in the male. In the second coupling, made in the attribute of the female, all the lights are incorporated there in the female. For this reason, some of the lights are incorporated in the male and some in the female. (page 357, and in Inner Light, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 103:1
items.html: (to question) See above answer 102.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 104:1
items.html: (to question) The departure of the first expansion is regarded as one departure, at once, since only one vessel was made there, and all five levels that emerged there due to the refinement of the screen are regarded as one light. Here, however, in the second expansion, the vessels precede the lights. This is because all the vessels with the sparks and the records in the first expansion, moved to the discernments of the vessels of the second expansion, and were placed one under the other even before the light of the second expansion returned to the Partzuf. Hence, each and every vessel here is considered a separate matter in itself. When the couplings of ZON are made in Malchut of the Rosh, and the level of Hochma descends to the Partzuf, she becomes completely clothed in the vessel of Keter, and the light does not expand in any other vessel. Hence, the vessel of Keter is considered a special Partzuf, having its own expansion and its own departure, and similarly in the rest of the vessels. Hence, the vessel of Keter became qualified to return to its coarseness and its coupling through the ascent of the lights of HB in a way that will be explained below in answer 105. However, the vessel of Keter of the first expansion is connected with the nine lower Sefirot into one degree and one discernment. There is no difference between the vessels of HB and the vessel of Keter since all of them together are only one light clothed in one vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 105:1
items.html: Each branch that is emanated and emerges from its root is in its greatest wholeness during the process of its emanation, before it is separated and comes to its own authority and degree. This is because then it is in the place of its root and is considered a part of it, in the form of eating what its mother eats. However, afterwards, when it comes down to its place, it is diminished and grows smaller according to its property. This creates a permanent connection between each branch and its root, where the root tends to enhance its branch to the same measure while it was in it before it descended to its place. This first beginning was rooted in the root, and it wishes to keep it always. Yet, because of the Katnut [smallness/infancy] of the vessels of the branch, they cannot receive the bestowal of the root; they receive only according to their ability. Hence, when the branch rises to its root once more, it awakens the root to extend itself to the same lights it had when it emanated it, and to adapt itself to the branch until it can bestow upon it all that Gadlut [greatness/adulthood] it bestowed upon it since the beginning of its creation. This is the meaning of ascents of MAN. It means that it awakens new lights in its root because of its ascent to it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 105:2
items.html: You already know that there are two kinds of turnings of the face downward during the emanation of a lower degree: The first is the turning of the face of the vessel that the Keter canceled its discernment of anterior, which was only to bestow VAK. It raised its posterior, which was for bestowal of GAR, and made it into anterior in order to emanate the male of the vessel of Hochma. The second is the turning of the face of the discernment of the screen, meaning refinement from the great coarseness to the lesser coarseness, meaning the refinement of phase three of the female of Keter to phase two, which is the level of Bina, who did that for the female of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 105:3
items.html: (to question) Thus, when ZON of Hochma, too, were refined from phase two to phase one, and the coupling for their level stopped from them, the same two kinds of turning of the face occurred in the vessel of Hochma to emanate ZON of Bina. You find that the vessel of Hochma, too, acquired the discernment of anterior of VAK, like the vessel of Keter. This equivalence of form returned the lights of HB to the vessel of Keter, and then the vessel of Keter, too, returned its anterior of illumination of VAK to its place as in the beginning. In order to shine to its branches, to ZON of Hochma, with whom they now united as in the beginning of their emanation, before they came down to their place, ZON of Keter corrected their screen once more in coarseness of phase three and phase four as in the beginning. They drew the same two couplings of theirs above in the Rosh, and bestowed their lights to the designated branches with which they are connected. This is called “raising MAN.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 106:1
items.html: (to question) The matter of the ascent to Malchut of the Rosh means equivalence with Malchut of the Rosh. This is only after the screen had been completely refined from all its coarseness. Hence, in all these exits and entries that were in the second expansion, before the light expanded to Malchut, the screen was still not refined completely. This is because until it expanded to Hod, it still had coarseness of phase one, and when it expanded to Yesod it still had root coarseness, which draws the level of Malchut. Therefore, it is still in disparity of form from Malchut of the Rosh. However, after it expanded to the vessel of Malchut, it was refined completely, like the discernment of Malchut of the Rosh. At that time, it rose to Malchut of the Rosh and the couplings for the Partzuf below it, called SAG, were made there, since the ascents of all the lights to the Rosh always elicit another Partzuf, which is a son of the previous Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 107:1
items.html: (to question) They are the vessels of the first expansion of AK. Before him, there was no clothing in the worlds. (page 293, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “These”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 108:1
items.html: (to question) The refinement of the screen from the discernment of coarseness in the vessel causes the cancelation of the vessel because it is unfit to receive any light when it lacks a screen. Also, the return of the light of Keter, as it was in the first expansion, causes the cancelation of the vessels, because the vessels mix with the lights. (There, in Inner Light, the passage beginning “The light”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 109:1
items.html: (to question) They were collected from many discernments: 1. From the vessels that were emptied in the first departure, and were arranged here one below the other, Keter first, Hochma next, and so on, and finally Malchut. These are primarily vessels of males, although the females, too, were incorporated there with the males. 2. The sparks from the striking of the records with the descending reflected light that fell into those vessels, as written in Part 4. These are primarily vessels of females, but the males, too, were incorporated with them. 3. The vessels of the light of Hochma itself. After Malchut of the Rosh drew the level of Hochma of the Rosh, she expanded once more from above downward into ten Sefirot from her and within her to her Malchut, called Chazeh. 4. These are the vessels that were made by the striking of the light of the record and the light of Hochma on each other. The vessels for GAR were made from their sparks. 5. These are the vessels that were made anew in the second expansion itself by the second departure here in ten exits of Lo Mati. However, they belong to Partzuf SAG.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 110:1
items.html: (to question) All the vessels that were emptied from the lights of Partzuf AB, moved to Partzuf SAG by the very same ways explained above in answer 109 regarding the transference of the vessels of the first expansion to the second expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 111:1
items.html: (to question) Since there were no strikings here to elicit sparks for the female, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 112:1
items.html: (to question) Because that coupling which is made on the discernments of records called ZON of the vessel of Keter was at nearly the level of Keter. Hence, they could only come down and clothe in their designated vessel, which is the vessel of Keter. However, after they were refined, and their level was diminished to the level of the other Sefirot, they descended and clothed in them to that extent. (page 318, Inner Light, the passage beginning “And in this”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 113:1
items.html: (to question) A place of bestowal is called anterior, and the place through which it does not bestow is called posterior. It makes no difference if that place is bestowal of GAR or bestowal of VAK. (page 325, Inner Light, the passage beginning “And the explanation”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 114:1
items.html: (to question) Because this was their beginning when they were made in the first departure, where Keter is above everyone, and Malchut is in the end.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 115:1
items.html: (to question) The anterior of the vessel of Keter is illumination of VAK that prevents GAR, and the posterior is illumination of GAR. The anterior of the vessel of Hochma is illumination of GAR, and the posterior is illumination of VAK. The anterior of the vessel of Bina is illumination of VAK, which is Hassadim, but it depends on the reason, as in “because He desires mercy.” If there is illumination of Hassadim in the Partzuf, the reason is canceled, and then she cancels her posterior. The anterior of the vessel of Hesed is illumination of GAR and his posterior is illumination of VAK since it is extended from the illumination of Hochma and resembles it. The anterior of Gevura is illumination of VAK, and her posterior GAR. This is because she is extended from the illumination of the vessel of Bina and resembles her. The anterior of Tifferet is a mixture of illumination of Hesed and Gevura together, meaning from the discernment of Gevura when she is incorporated in the anterior of Hesed, and his posterior is illumination of VAK. The anterior of Netzah is illumination of VAK and his posterior is illumination of GAR. The anterior of Hod is illumination of GAR, and his posterior is illumination of VAK. The anterior of Yesod is illumination of VAK, and his posterior is illumination of GAR. The anterior of Malchut is illumination of GAR. (There, the passage beginning “And the explanation,” throughout the continuation)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 116:1
items.html: (to question) This is because a vessel is not completed before the light moves three distances from it. Because of this, only the vessels of ZON were completed, and they move to the next Partzuf, where the light returns in the same empty vessels. Thus, the vessels that were made in second observation of the Partzuf are only for the needs of the second Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 117:1
items.html: (to question) In the first expansion, there was only one expansion and one departure, though it departed gradually. However, in the second expansion, it expanded by an order of Mati and Lo Mati, creating ten exits and ten entries until it expanded to Malchut. (page 307, item 20)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 118:1
items.html: (to question) The vessels of GAR, which are KHB, were made by the second expansion itself, since the light of Hochma dressed there in the vessel of Keter, and the light of the male of Keter clothes inside the light of Hochma. By this, the inferior light falls from within the record and becomes a vessel below the light of Hochma, as the light of Hochma clothes in it. It follows, that Hochma separates between the light of the record, which is the male of Keter, and the inferior light that was separated from him, and by this, the vessel of Keter becomes very dark, and in that state, its discernment of the vessel is finished. The vessels of Hochma and Bina were made similarly. (page 347, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 119:1
items.html: (to question) There are three causes here: 1. Because of the division and the departure of the superior light of the record from the inferior light in it. 2. Because of the coming of the light of Hochma in the middle, separating between the superior light of the record and the inferior light that was separated from it. 3. Because of the posterior of the root light of Keter that did not return for the second expansion. It remained standing under Malchut of the Rosh with its posterior to the branches, meaning to the Sefirot of the Guf. This posterior of the light of Keter diminishes the light extensively and darken the Sefirot KHB even more than they had during first departure itself. For this reason, they darken the vessels as if the light is at a distance of three degrees. (page 349, the passage beginning “And behold, the ARI”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 120:1
items.html: (to question) They are the discernments that exist in the externality of the vessel. They are not as coarse as the inner half of the wall. For example, if the internality of the vessel is phase four, and the level of Keter departs from it, the externality of the vessel, which is phase three, is fit to receive more light from the illumination of the coupling of its upper discernment, which is the level of phase three. Also, her phase two is fit to receive more of the illumination of coupling in the degree above the upper degree. (page 304, item 15)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 121:1
items.html: (to question) When the light departs from the degree, and the coupling is made in the degree above it, such as when the light departs from phase three, and the coupling is done in phase two, the reflected light descends from the illumination of the coupling of phase two to the lower phase three. At that time, there is a clash between the record of phase three and the descending reflected light. This is so because the illumination of phase two is in oppositeness to the record of phase three. At that time, the record leaves its place and rises above the vessel, giving room to the reflected light to clothe in the vessel of phase three. Thus, this reflected light clothes the outer half of the wall of that vessel, which fits its measure of level, which is in phase two that is in phase three, which is the posterior of phase three. You find that the anterior of phase three remains empty of light, and the posterior of phase three, which is phase two, is filled with light. This is called turning its posterior upward, and its anterior downward. It follows that the reflected light that descends from the illumination of the coupling of the upper degree, causes the vessel of the lower degree to turn its anterior downward. (page 305, Inner Light, the passage beginning “And every”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 122:1
items.html: (to question) After the coupling stops from the adjacent upper degree, as well, and the reflected light that descends to the vessel stops, the record returns into her vessel. Thus, the vessel returns its anterior upward, and its posterior downward as in the beginning. This is because now the posterior of the vessel cannot receive the illumination of the record, which is phase three, and it returns to being externality of the vessel as in the beginning, and all the illumination of record comes to anterior of the vessel, which is phase three. (page 306, Inner Light, the passage beginning “That the light”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 123:1
items.html: (to question) When the light departs from the vessel and the coupling is made in the degree above it, such as when it departs from phase three, and the coupling is made in phase two, then the posterior of this vessel, which is phase two, looks at the upper light, meaning receives from the illumination of the coupling that is there. (Inner Light, item 15, the passage beginning “Looks”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 124:1
items.html: (to question) Their levels equalize with one another and they are back-to-back by the refinement of the coarseness and the turning of the anterior downward. (page 319, Inner Light, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 125:1
items.html: An upper degree cannot bestow upon the lower one except through equivalence with it, for then they are close to one another. Therefore, there is here the matter of the upper one turning its face to the measure of the face of the lower one, called face to face. There are two discernments of turning the face. The first is that every vessel is defined by its natural discernment of bestowal—whether illumination of VAK or illumination of GAR. The vessel of Keter naturally bestows VAK and not GAR. Therefore, when it bestows upon Hochma, whose face is GAR, Keter must turn its face downward and its posterior upward to become its face, in order to equalize its face with the face of Hochma. The same applies to the rest of the Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 125:2
items.html: (to question) The second is equivalence of level, which is also called turning the face downward. For example, the level of Keter cannot bestow upon the degree of Hochma except through the refinement of the coarseness of phase four into phase three, which draws the level of Hochma. Then the level of Keter is equal to the degree of Hochma, and Keter bestows its illumination upon Hochma. (page 325, Inner Light, the passage beginning “Therefore”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 126:1
items.html: (to question) It is the turning of the face of the vessel of Hochma downward and the making of the posterior, which is illumination of VAK, into her anterior, like the anterior of the vessel of Bina. By so doing, Hochma was divided into two discernments, meaning bestowal of GAR and bestowal of VAK. The vessel Hochma itself is considered bestowal of GAR, and the vessel of Bina, which received VAK of Hochma, is considered bestowal of VAK. (page 326, Inner Light, the passage beginning “And remember”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 127:1
items.html: (to question) This is because once the coupling stops from the highest discernment, from the vessel whose light has been emptied, the record returns to her place and the vessel returns its anterior to its place as in the beginning, as it is written in answer 122 above. Hence, all the vessels remain in the discernment of anterior and posterior after the completion of the departure, meaning the anterior of the lower one in the posterior of the upper one. (page 307, item 18)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 128:1
items.html: (to question) Because phase four did not leave a record. It is known that phase four serves as anterior to the vessel of Keter, which is the coarsest in the screen, called anterior. That which is not so coarse is considered the posterior of Keter. It is considered that its anterior is downward, and equalizes with the anterior of Hochma since it has become close to phase three of Hochma. Even though a record of phase four of clothing remains there, it is not enough to return the anterior of the vessel of Keter as in the beginning. Also, this causes the light of Keter to remain in the Peh, and not return in the second expansion. (Inner Light, item 18, the passage beginning “The Keter”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 129:1
items.html: (to question) Because the vessel lacks its primary record, which is a record of extension, and the record of clothing that remains in it is considered the posterior of the vessel of Keter. Also, her light up in the Rosh stands with its posterior to the branches in the Guf. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 130:1
items.html: (to question) See in Inner Observation, at the end of Part 1. It explains there that spiritual time is considered motion, and spiritual motion is considered an innovation of form that is attained there. From this we understand that the slightest innovation of form, the slightest of the slightest of changes, is called a “moment.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 131:1
items.html: (to question) When the light of Malchut rose to the vessel of Hochma, a distance of three degrees was made between the light and the vessel, and the vessel was darkened, and then it was completed. (page 306, item 17, and Inner Light, the passage beginning “Until it becomes distant”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 132:1
items.html: (to question) When light of ZA rose to its root to the Rosh, a distance of three degrees without light has been made between the light and the vessel; hence, the vessel was darkened and completed (There), see below, answer 134.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 133:1
items.html: (to question) This is so because up to three degrees, the vessel still receives from surrounding lights. This is so because when the light of Malchut ascends to ZA, Malchut receives one surrounding. When it rises to Bina, she receives a second surrounding, but when the light of Malchut rises to the vessel of Hochma, it no longer receives any illumination; hence, the vessel becomes dark and is completed. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 134:1
items.html: (to question) As long as there is some light in a vessel, even though it is not from its own discernment, it is not regarded as remoteness of degree. Hence, when the light of ZA rises to the vessel of Bina, at which time the light of Malchut rises to the vessel of ZA, it is still considered having inner light in its vessel. However, afterwards, when the light of ZA rose to the vessel of Hochma, it is regarded as remoteness of one degree. When it rises to the vessel of Keter, it is considered remoteness of two degrees, when the vessel still receives from surrounding lights, and has still not become completely dark. Only when it rises to the Emanator is it completely darkened and its vessel is completed. (page 347, item 50, and page 311, item 27)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 135:1
items.html: (to question) In the departure of the lights of the first expansion, called Partzuf Keter. For this reason, it is called the departure of the light of Keter. (page 294, item 6, Inner Light, the passage beginning “Lo Mati”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 136:1
items.html: (to question) See answer 135 above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 137:1
items.html: (to question) The clash and striking of surrounding light in inner light. (page 294, the passage beginning “Lo Mati”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 138:1
items.html: (to question) Because with respect to the vessel itself, there is only one refinement and one departure here. This is so because in the end, there is only a vessel Malchut here, and no vessels were added to the vessel Malchut by all those departures. The ten Sefirot that we discern in it are like one long vessel that contains ten parts that are not equal to each other. (page 308, item 22, and Inner Light, the passage beginning “Yod”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 139:1
items.html: (to question) Because at the moment of expansion to Malchut and the light departs completely from the Partzuf, it immediately returned to expand in Keter, until the disappearance of the light was like a flame that sways here and there. (page 345, the passage beginning “The measure”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 140:1
items.html: (to question) Although they are regarded as one level, the level of phase two, they are still related as VAK relates to GAR. This is because ZON of Hochma are considered GAR, and ZON of Bina are considered VAK of GAR. It is like YESHSUT of Atzilut compared to AVI of Atzilut. The male of the vessel of Bina was born from the coupling of ZON of Hochma when they turned their anterior downward, meaning when they canceled the illumination of GAR in them and received the anterior of VAK. Hence, the male was born in the discernment of posterior of Hochma, and in the discernment of VAK. The female of Bina is the discernment of GAR, which is a record of the light of Bina of the first expansion. Nevertheless, since she is a record without light, who receives all the light in her through the male, which is VAK, for this reason, the force of the male is on her. Also, the vessel of Bina itself is also the discernment of VAK of GAR, as in “because He desires mercy.” Thus, ZON of Bina are considered the discernment of VAK of GAR. (page 326, the passage beginning “And remember”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 141:1
items.html: (to question) Initially, it was Lo Mati in Keter. Due to the clash of surrounding light and inner light on each other, the ZON of Keter were refined, which are phase four and phase three, to phase three and phase two. They gave them to the Hochma in the discernments of ZON of Hochma, and then the anterior of Hochma returned to their place as in the beginning. Hence, ZON of Bina rose once more to Hochma since VAK always join their GAR when they are revealed. Thus, now Hochma joined with Bina into one degree. Consequently, the light Hesed, which is in the vessel of Bina, now receives illumination of Hochma because of their unification of Hochma and Bina. Hesed became great because it acquired illumination of Hochma. This means that it no longer needs to suckle illumination of GAR from the vessel of Bina, and can expand into its own degree, and ZON of Bina were refined into phase one in order to equalize with the vessel of Hesed, and the light of Hesed was lowered to the vessel of Hesed. (page 327, the passage beginning “Explanation”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 142:1
items.html: (to question) It is the discernment of Keter of the five discernments of light of Hassadim, since KHB of the light of Hassadim is called HGT. (page 328, the passage beginning “Now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 143:1
items.html: (to question) It is evaluated as the discernment of light of Hochma in the vessel of Keter. This is because Hesed has only that illumination of Hochma that the general light of Hesed received while being in the vessel of Bina. Also, everything that is found in the general light of Hesed below the light of Hochma that it received, no longer belongs to the Sefira Hesed, but to the six lower Sefirot below Hesed. Hence, Hesed is considered the discernment of Hochma in the vessel of Keter, since its vessel is the discernment of Keter, as written above in answer 142. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 144:1
items.html: (to question) This is the rule: The coming of the light of Hesed to its vessel causes an expansion in Keter. This is because then the ZON of Bina were refined to phase one in order to be face-to-face with the vessel of the Hesed. For this reason, the entire level of the light of Bina disappeared, and the four lights of HB rose to Keter. At that time, they cause there a new coupling and expansion in Keter. You find that the posterior of Keter returned to its place as in the beginning, and illumination of GAR was denied of the entire Partzuf. Since the illumination of GAR stopped from the light of Hesed, it immediately becomes needy of its mother Bina, in order to suckle illumination of GAR from the vessel of Bina. Hence, it rises to Bina, and the vessel of Hesed turns its anterior downward, giving its residue, meaning everything below its own discernment, to vessel of Gevura. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 145:1
items.html: (to question) Her vessel has the relation of Hochma of the light of Hassadim since KHB of Hassadim are called HGT, and her light is the discernment of VAK of illumination of Hochma in Hesed, which is as VAK of GAR compared to the light of Hesed. It is like the male of the vessel of Bina, which is the discernment of VAK of GAR compared to Hochma, as written in answer 140 above. Thus, the quality of the light of Gevura compared to the light Hesed is as the value of ZON of Bina compared to ZON of Hochma. This is the meaning of “I am Bina [understanding], Gevura [strength] is mine,” since their value is equal to each other, and there is no difference between them, but only in the measure of the level. One is the level of phase two, and one is the level of phase one. (page 325, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 146:1
items.html: (to question) See answer 145 above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 147:1
items.html: (to question) After it returned to being Lo Mati [not reaching] in Keter, its posterior was canceled on the GAR, and ZON of Hochma returned to their place, the vessel of Hochma turned its anterior without refinement and placed ZON of Bina to their place. After that, ZON of Bina returned to phase one, and lowered the light of Hesed to its place. This is because after the illumination of GAR returned to the Partzuf, and Hesed acquired illumination of Hochma, it no longer needs its mother Bina. At that time, the light of Gevura rises to Hesed, since when the GAR reappears, its VAK immediately joins with it. In that state, the vessel of Gevura turns its anterior downward and places its residue, meaning everything that is below the discernment of the light of Gevura, to the vessel of Tifferet. (page 328, the passage beginning “Now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 148:1
items.html: (to question) Its vessel is the discernment of Bina of the light of Hassadim. Its light is the self of the light of Hesed that was in the vessel of Bina. This is because the lights of Hesed and Gevura are only illuminations of GAR and VAK of Hochma that the light of Hesed received, but Tifferet is this light of Hassadim itself. The value of the Sefira is as the value of the Daat that copulates between Hochma and Bina, since it is the discernment of the light of Hesed in the vessel of Bina, which is the light of Daat. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 149:1
items.html: (to question) The difference is in the value, like the difference between the lower Daat and the upper Daat. When the light of Hesed is in Bina, it unites the HB into one Partzuf, in the sense that it receives the illumination of Hochma from the time when Hochma and Bina returned to one Partzuf. When it is in Tifferet, it is in the form of the lower Daat, uniting the lights Hesed and Gevura into one in the sense that it receives illumination of Hesed from the time when Gevura rose to Hesed and united with it into one light. Because of that beginning, the uniting of Hochma and Gevura into one has been imprinted in it forever, since it cannot receive its abundance from them in another way. It is like upper Daat, which cannot receive illumination of Hochma, except through Hochma and Bina, into one Partzuf. (page 330, the passage beginning “Now it is understood”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 150:1
items.html: (to question) It is a new upshot that emerged during the concealment of the light of Keter from Partzuf AB and the replacement of the lights. Because the light of Hochma clothed in the vessel of Keter, the light of ZA ascended to clothe in the vessel of Bina to be emanated by the Hochma. In so doing, two discernments of light of ZA were emanated: The first relates to Partzuf Keter, when the lights are in their actual place, at which time ZA was emanated by Bina, clothing in the vessels of VAK. The second relates to Partzuf Hochma, when the lights swapped their places. At that time, the light of ZA was emanated by Hochma, clothing in the vessels of GAR, meaning the vessel of Bina. Hence, from here on, all the Partzufim contain two discernments of ZA in each Partzuf, where the upper ZA, which acquired a place of GAR, is called the Sefira Daat, and the lower ZA, which stands in its actual place in VAK, is called ZA. (page 331, the passage beginning “And behold, it has been explained”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 151:1
items.html: (to question) From the perspective of the light, which is the primary, the Sefira Tifferet is the primary part of ZA, since the light of Tifferet is the self of the light Hesed in the vessel of Bina. For this reason, it is called Vav with a Rosh, as discernments GAR of Bina rest on it from the time it was in the vessel of Bina. However, from the perspective of the vessel, it is the Sefira Netzah, which is the fourth edge in the five edges, opposite the fourth discernment in the five discernments KHB, ZA, and Malchut. You find that ZA in the five discernments is opposite Netzah in the five Hassadim. (There, the passage beginning “And in every”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 152:1
items.html: (to question) Hesed and Gevura, which are opposite HB, are the discernment of the Rosh of the ZAT. Tifferet and Netzah are the discernment of Toch of the ZAT. One is from the perspective of the light, and the other is from the perspective of the vessel, as in answer 151 above. Hod, Yesod, Malchut, are the discernment of Sof of the ZAT since Hod is the fifth edge of the five edges, corresponding to Malchut in the five discernments, and Yesod and Malchut are extended from it. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 153:1
items.html: (to question) Hesed and Gevura are not the self of the light of Hesed, but illuminations of Hochma and Bina that reached Hesed when it clothed in the vessel of Bina. But Tifferet is the self and essence of the light of Hesed. (page 331, the passage beginning “Therefore”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 154:1
items.html: (to question) It is because of the property of their vessels. The vessels of Hesed and Gevura are the discernment of Keter and Hochma, in which the light of Hesed has no root because it only clothed the vessel of Bina of GAR. For this reason, the self of the light of Hesed cannot clothe in the discernment of the five Hassadim, but rather in the vessel of Tifferet, which is Bina of the five Hassadim, and not in Hesed and Gevura, which are Keter and Hochma of the five Hassadim. The light of Hesed never clothed in Keter and Hochma, and therefore, the vessels of Hesed and Gevura only have illuminations of Hochma and Bina that reached the reception of the light of Hesed when it was in the vessel of Bina, and the self of the light of Hesed clothed in the vessel of Tifferet. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 155:1
items.html: (to question) When it is Mati in Keter once again, when the control of the posterior of Keter returns as in the beginning, and illumination of GAR is denied from the entire Partzuf, the light of Hesed departs to Bina once more, its VAK expands in Gevura, and the light of Tifferet also departs and returns to its root in the vessel of Gevura, and gives its VAK to the vessel of Netzah and expands in Netzah. (page 332, the passage beginning “Returned”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 156:1
items.html: (to question) The vessel is the self of ZA since it is the fourth edge, opposite ZA of the five discernments. Its light is the discernment of VAK from the self of the light of ZA, which is the light of Tifferet. After the light of Tifferet concealed in its root, in Gevura, Tifferet gave its VAK to Netzah, as it is written in answer 155 above. (page 332, the passage beginning “Now we will understand”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 157:1
items.html: (to question) Even though every discernment of seven lower Sefirot is the discernment of VAK, they still have illumination of GAR in them. Hence, as we discern two discernments in GAR, GAR of VAK and VAK of GAR, so we have two discernments in VAK: GAR of VAK and VAK of VAK. This is so because HGT are considered GAR of VAK, and NHY are VAK of VAK. For this reason, NHY are considered outside the Guf, as they are the discernment of light of Hassadim, which lack illumination of Hochma, and the entire vitality of the Guf is only light of Hochma since it is the self of the upper light. However, it is impossible for NHY to be completely empty of illumination of Hochma since they would be completely canceled. Instead, there is a discernment of a record of HGT in them, which means a small illumination, and for this reason, the NHY are called three inside three, which means that the records of the three Sefirot HGT are concealed in the three Sefirot NHY in a way that suffices for their persistence.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 158:1
items.html: (to question) The vessel is the discernment of Hesed, the fifth of the five Hassadim in the five discernments, meaning phase four, which is the quality of judgment. However, she is from the perspective of her being incorporated in ZA, and her light is the residue of Netzah. However, from the perspective of the incorporation of Netzah in Tifferet, when the light Netzah is incorporated in illumination of GAR, as well, from the discernment of the light of Daat that shines in Tifferet, hence, the light of Hod is considered merely the discernment of illumination of GAR of the light of Daat, and nothing of the illumination of GAR of Hochma and Bina. This is so because its entire illumination is extended from the connection of GAR and VAK of the light of Tifferet, meaning the connection of Netzah with Tifferet after the illumination of GAR is extended to the Partzuf. You already know that the light of Tifferet is merely the light Daat, and not from Hochma and Bina, whose place is in the vessels of Hesed and Gevura. (There)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 159:1
items.html: (to question) Its vessel is from the discernment of Malchut since it is extended from Hod, which is the root of Malchut of the five Hassadim, and the light in it is made of both judgment and mercy. This is so because it has two lights: The first is the residue of the light that Hod gave it, which is the level of Malchut, which is the discernment of judgment. The second light is the Hey that reached it from the coupling of ZON of Bina that the Hod illuminated for before it was refined to the level of Malchut. (page 336, the passage beginning “In such a way”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 160:1
items.html: (to question) The light of Malchut clothed in the vessel of Yesod. This is because after the Hod was refined from phase one to the discernment of Keter, the level that emerges on that screen has only the level of Malchut, and then he gives it to the vessel of Yesod. (page 338, the passage beginning “And behold”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 161:1
items.html: (to question) The light of the Dalet that surrounds the truncated Vav inside the Hey, which reached the Yesod from the coupling of ZON of Bina, which is the discernment of GAR without VAK, meaning without light of Hassadim, descended from Yesod and clothed in Malchut. (page 341, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 162:1
items.html: (to question) See answer 140 above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 163:1
items.html: (to question) They are four discernments of ZON: ZON of the vessel of Keter, ZON of the vessel of Hochma, ZON of the vessel of Bina, and ZON of the vessel of Yesod and Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 164:1
items.html: (to question) In the first two pairs, which are ZON of Keter and ZON of Hochma, the males are more important than the females. This is because the male of Keter is from phase four of clothing, but the female of Keter is only from phase three. The male of the vessel of Hochma is only from phase three, but the female of the vessel of Hochma is from phase two. Thus, the males are more important than the females. However, in ZON of the vessel of Bina, the female is greater than the male, since the male is the discernment of VAK of Hochma, and the female is the discernment of GAR, as she is a record of the light of Bina from the time of the first expansion. In ZON, however, which is in the vessel of Yesod, the male is greater than the female since the male is the truncated Vav inside the Hey, which is extended from the coupling of Bina, which is given to Yesod from the Sefira Hod without refinement, but only as illumination. Hence, it is the discernment of Hassadim of phase one, and is also extended from a high place, from the coupling of ZON of Bina. But the female in Yesod is the residue of the light of Hod after its GAR disappeared, and after it was refined from phase one to the level of Malchut. Thus, it is much lower than her male. (page 339, the passage beginning “And you find”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 165:1
items.html: (to question) When the light of Dalet in the Hey from the coupling of ZON of Bina is Mati in Malchut. This is so because the screen has been entirely refined from there from all its coarseness until it equalized with the discernment of Malchut of the Rosh, which is considered that it rose to the Rosh, to the Emanator. At that time, all the lights departed from the Partzuf. (page 340, the passage beginning “And the matter of Dalet”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 166:1
items.html: (to question) It is the discernment of perpetual Mati and Lo Mati. Every time the light is Mati in Malchut, it immediately becomes Mati in Keter, Gevura, Netzah, and Yesod, and Lo Mati in Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Tifferet, Hod, and Malchut. Afterwards, Keter returns to being Lo Mati, and it is Mati in Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Tifferet, Hod, and Malchut, and Lo Mati in Keter, Gevura, Netzah, and Yesod, and so on and so forth continually. This state of perpetual Mati and Lo Mati is called Partzuf SAG of AK, or Bina of AK. (page 340, the passage beginning “The second discernment”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 167:1
items.html: When it is Mati in Malchut of AB of AK, which is the first discernment of the second expansion, the screen is refined entirely, and equalizes with Malchut of the Rosh, since the equivalence of form unites the spirituals into one. That screen that rose to the Rosh consists of all the records of the Sefirot of the second expansion, which are five lights: ZON of Hochma and Bina, and the light of Hesed, which contains ZAT, which are all included in ZON of Keter. However, the record of phase three, which is coarseness of extension that was in the second expansion, and is the last discernment here, disappeared like the last discernment of Partzuf Keter. This is phase four that disappeared in the first departure there. The rule is that the last discernment does not leave a record, and this applies to every single departure. Hence, only the record of phase two remained here after the second departure. However, the discernment of the record of clothing of phase three remained, as well, as phase four of clothing remained after the first departure, since only the discernment of extension is lost from each last discernment, but not the discernment of clothing.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 167:2
items.html: (to question) Therefore, these two records there—phase three of clothing and phase two, which also contains the discernment of extension—caused two upper couplings in the Rosh, like the two couplings of ZON of Keter after the first departure, because they were incorporated in one another. In the first coupling, the female was incorporated in the male in phase three, and then a level of ten Sefirot emerged close to the level of the upper Hochma. However, they still could not expand and descend below to the Guf because phase three lacks extension.
