Afterwards, a second coupling was made, in which the male was incorporated in the female in phase two, and then ten Sefirot emerged at the level of Bina. Now that it also had the discernment of extension, Malchut of this level of Bina could expand within herself into ten Sefirot and descend to the Guf. Then the above ZON descended to the vessel of Keter of the Guf, filled with light from the two discernments of the above couplings. The constant matter of Mati and Lo Mati was made in them, so that whenever it was Mati in Malchut, they returned to Keter. As is known, this is called Partzuf SAG of AK. (See page 340, the passage beginning “The second discernment”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 168:1
items.html: (to question) The ZON of the vessels of KHB of AB of AK are all the discernment of Yod-Hey. The male of the vessel of Keter is the discernment of the record of phase four of clothing, and its light is extended from the first coupling in the Rosh, but it is also incorporated in the second coupling of the Rosh in the light of Hochma. The female of the vessel of Keter is the actual level of Hochma that expanded in Partzuf AB, and her light is from the second coupling of the Rosh, but she was also incorporated in the first coupling of the Rosh in the light of the upper Keter. Of the ZON of the vessel of Hochma, the male is from the male of Keter after it was refined to phase three, and the female is from the female of the vessel of Keter after she was refined to phase two. Every discernment of GAR in the Partzuf is extended only through these ZON of Hochma. Of the ZON of the vessel of Bina, the male was born from the coupling of ZON of Hochma after they turned their faces from GAR to illumination of VAK, and the female is the discernment of the record that remained in the vessel of Bina from the time of the first departure. (page 347, item 50, and page 349, item 51)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 169:1
items.html: (to question) They are all called Yod-Hey.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 170:1
items.html: (to question) Each of them is called the letter Yod in its filling: The male of the vessel of Keter is called Yod, the female, Vav, and the vessel of Keter, Dalet. Likewise, the male of Hochma is called Yod, the female, Vav, and the vessel of Hochma, Dalet. But in Bina there is a change, for the male is called Yod, the female is called Dalet, and the vessel does not rise in the name; rather, the light of Hesed within her is called Vav. (page 350, item 53)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 171:1
items.html: (to question) Four phases of ZON: three in KHB and one ZON in Yesod. (page 351, item 54)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 172:1
items.html: (to question) This means a light born through a coupling of ZON for the need of a lower degree. But giving lights means a light that cascades and descends from Sefira to Sefira through the refinement of the screen. (page 316, item 35)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 173:1
items.html: (to question) This is because the giving of the seven lights to Bina was through refinement to phase one. But the male of Bina, which was emanated through Hochma, was at the level of phase two, though from the discernment of posterior. Therefore, it bestowed it upon the vessel of Bina only by turning its face toward VAK, before it was refined to phase one.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 174:1
items.html: (to question) It is because of the posterior of the light of Keter that stands under Malchut of the Rosh and detains the bestowal of the light of Keter to the vessel of GAR. But after ZON of Keter were refined and the discernment of the light of Keter departed to its root, its posterior was annulled, and their remainder was given to the vessel of Hochma, which is ZON of the vessel of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 175:1
items.html: (to question) During the control of the posterior of Keter, which prevents illumination of GAR from the Partzuf, when the two Sefirot Hochma and Bina are without light, there is no illumination of GAR in Hesed. Therefore, it needs its mother, Bina, and rises to her to nurse GAR from the place of Bina. But when there is Mati [reaching] in the two Sefirot Hochma and Bina, there is illumination of GAR in the Partzuf and Hesed has illumination of Hochma. Then it does not need its mother and can descend and come to its own degree. (page 323, the passage beginning “The seven sons”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 176:1
items.html: (to question) This is because the revelation of illumination of GAR in the vessel of Hochma, just as it illuminated Gadlut to Hesed, also drew ZON of Bina to it, and it united with them into one Partzuf. Then Bina was refined from phase two to phase one in order to be face to face with the vessel of Hesed, and gave the light of Hesed there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 177:1
items.html: (to question) When Bina was refined from phase two to phase one to give the light of Hesed to the vessel of Hesed, at that time she gave there, together with the light of Hesed, the Hey that was born from her coupling. Hesed gave it to Gevura as illumination alone before it departed to the vessel of Bina, and likewise Gevura to Tifferet, and so forth, until it reached its place in Yesod. He took the Vav within her and gave the Dalet to Malchut. (page 335, item 44, and in Inner Light there, the passage beginning “And likewise”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 178:1
items.html: (to question) The light of Hesed is the discernment of the light of the anterior, whose illumination is from the discernment of the anterior of Hochma, and the beginning of its emanation was also through ZON of Hochma. But the Hey is from the discernment of posterior, for she was emanated through ZON of the vessel of Bina, which are the discernment of VAK of Hochma. Yet she contains the discernment of GAR from the record of Bina. However, these GAR are dark because they are from the discernment of departure, and therefore they are subordinate to the VAK of the male. (page 334, the passage beginning “And now you will understand”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 179:1
items.html: (to question) When illumination of GAR returned to the Partzuf and there was Mati in Hod, at which time the light of Yesod departed and rose to its root, to the illumination of GAR in Hod, the truncated Vav rose with it while they were united with one another, and the light of the Dalet descended to Malchut. (page 338, the passage beginning “And behold the secret”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 180:1
items.html: (to question) Since the difference between VAK and GAR is very great, it is utterly impossible for the light of Hesed, which is complete VAK, to be a male to the discernment of Bina, which is GAR. (page 349, the passage beginning “For the light”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 181:1
items.html: (to question) This is because the light of Hesed, which is ZA, is male from its origin in direct light, and a male does not invert to become a female. Moreover, VAK and GAR cannot be on one degree. (ibid.)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 182:1
items.html: (to question) The letter Dalet of the Hey of the coupling of ZON of Bina completed Malchut of AB, which has no light. (page 351, item 54)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 183:1
items.html: (to question) The Vav of the Hey of the coupling of Bina that descended to Yesod is the male of Yesod, and the light of Malchut that it received from the remainder of Hod is the female. (page 351, item 54)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 184:1
items.html: (to question) Since she is only the discernment of the record remaining from the time of the first departure and is without light, she therefore equalizes with the male extended from the coupling of ZON of Hochma, which is full of light. (page 337, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 185:1
items.html: (to question) Two lights contain all the degrees: the light of Hochma and the light of Hassadim. Therefore, the five discernments called KHB, ZA and Malchut are called by these names only when they are light of Hochma. But when they are light of Hassadim, they are called HGT NH, or five Hassadim, or five ends. This is when they have the level of the light of phase one. But when they have only the light of Malchut, they are called five Gevurot. (page 355, the passage beginning “And now we will explain”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 186:1
items.html: Two lights are found in Yesod: One is the discernment of the truncated Vav, which is extended to it from the coupling of ZON of Bina. The second is the discernment of the light of Malchut that came to it from the remainder of Hod after it was refined from phase one within it to the level of Malchut. From this refinement, the five Hassadim were divided into two discernments, namely the level of phase one and the level of Malchut. They are called five Hassadim when they are at the level of phase one, and they are called five Gevurot when they are at the level of Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 186:2
items.html: (to question) Since Yesod received the level of Malchut, it follows that Yesod received all five Gevurot together. It follows that all five ends are incorporated in it in the discernment of five Gevurot, which came to it from the remainder of Hod after it was diminished to the level of Malchut. Therefore, Yesod is called the incorporation of the five ends, since they are all in it in the forms of Gevurot, as explained above. However, these five Gevurot in Yesod are sweetened in the light of Hassadim of the truncated Vav that it received from ZON of Bina. This Vav received from Hod before it was refined to the level of Malchut, and therefore it is still in the measure of the level of phase one. Consequently, the five Gevurot in Yesod are sweetened in the light of Hassadim in this Vav. It therefore follows that only in Yesod are the five Hassadim and five Gevurot found sweetened together. (page 338, the passage beginning “And behold the secret”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 187:1
items.html: (to question) Two levels, which are nearly the level of Keter and the level of Hochma, called ZON, were extended through two couplings of Malchut of the Rosh, expanded and descended to the vessel of Keter of Partzuf AB, called the second expansion. They contain all the Sefirot below them in this Partzuf. (page 318, the passage beginning “Therefore”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 188:1
items.html: (to question) Because the posterior of the light of Keter, which remained in the Rosh and did not return to the Guf, prevents illumination of GAR from the Partzuf. Therefore, as long as its record shines by the force of its illumination in the vessel of Keter, there is Lo Mati [not reaching] in Hochma and Bina, since they are from the discernment of illumination of GAR. (page 324, the passage beginning “And we must understand”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 189:1
items.html: (to question) This is because the lights of Bina are only VAK, which were emanated through the posterior of Hochma when it turned its face downward. Therefore, when there is Mati in Hochma and the face of the vessel of Hochma returns to its place as in the beginning, ZON of Bina immediately return to their discernment of GAR, to the vessel of Hochma. For VAK and GAR that come from one degree are separated from one another only by a cause that compels them to it, and therefore, when the cause is annulled, they immediately return to their place. (page 327, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 190:1
items.html: (to question) This is because Bina cannot bestow the light of Hesed before she is refined to phase one and before she turns her face downward. For this turning of the face, the light of Bina must depart from the vessel of Bina, and there is Lo Mati in Bina. Therefore, as long as there is Mati in Bina, there is Lo Mati in Hesed. (page 323, the passage beginning “And then”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 191:1
items.html: (to question) Light of Hassadim with illumination of Hochma is Mati in the vessel of Hesed, and only illumination of Hochma alone is attributed to Hesed. Everything below this illumination of Hochma it gives to Gevura. Light of Hassadim in itself, with illumination of GAR through Gevura’s return to Hesed, is Mati in the vessel of Tifferet. (page 327, the passage beginning “Now,” and page 332, the passage beginning “Now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 192:1
items.html: (to question) Two levels: nearly the level of Hochma and the level of Bina, called ZON. They were extended through two couplings in Malchut of the Rosh, expanded and descended from there to the vessel of Keter of Partzuf SAG. (page 340, the passage beginning “And we will explain”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 193:1
items.html: (to question) ZON of the vessel of Hochma of SAG were emanated through the turning of the face of the vessel of Keter, and relative to ZON of Keter they are the discernment of VAK. However, all the illumination of GAR of Partzuf Bina comes from these ZON, and it is by the force of the record of the light of Bina that remained in the vessel of Hochma from the time of the second expansion. The relation of these ZON of Hochma is similar to the relation of ZON of Bina of Partzuf AB. (page 341, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 194:1
items.html: (to question) They contain the records of the vessel of Bina of Partzuf AB and receive their illumination from ZON of the vessel of Hochma. (page 341, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 195:1
items.html: (to question) The light of Hassadim with illumination of Bina, and the Hey from the coupling of ZON of the vessel of Hochma. (page 342, the passage beginning “And one should not ask”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 196:1
items.html: (to question) This is because when illumination of GAR is Mati in the vessel of Hod, the light of Yesod, which is the discernment of VAK of this light, returns to it. (ibid.)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 197:1
items.html: (to question) This is because the light of Hochma that remained in the Rosh and did not return to this expansion of SAG turns its posterior toward its branches in the vessel of Keter. Because of this posterior of Hochma, ZON of Keter cannot bestow the discernment of GAR upon the Partzuf. Therefore, when the light is Mati in Keter, illumination of GAR is prevented from the entire Partzuf, and only the vessels from the discernment of VAK—Gevura, Netzah and Yesod—shine. There is Lo Mati in Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Tifferet, Hod and Malchut because their faces are the discernment of GAR. (page 342, the passage beginning “And now we will explain”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 198:1
items.html: (to question) This is because in every Sefira where illumination of GAR is Mati, its VAK, which are in the Sefira below it, immediately return to it. When there is Mati in HB, at which time illumination of GAR returns to the Partzuf and there is Mati in Hesed, its VAK in Gevura return to it. Then there is Mati in Tifferet and the VAK in Netzah return to it; there is Mati in Hod and the VAK in Yesod return to Hod; and there is Mati in Malchut. (page 342, the passage beginning “And there is not”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 199:1
items.html: The reason for the refinement of the screen of phase two is that this screen relies on the posterior of Bina, which stops Hochma, in the secret of Yod Nun of Tzadi, which are inverted from one another. These posterior of Bina depend on a cause and are not because of Bina herself, for Bina is the self of Hochma. This posterior of hers is because Bina of direct light craves Hassadim, in the secret of “for He desires mercy.” Therefore, so that she could draw Hassadim, she turned her posterior toward the light of Hochma. It follows that the lack of Hassadim is the cause of the posterior of Bina.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 199:2
items.html: Therefore, when the coupling was made on the screen of phase two and the splendour was bestowed upon the Partzuf, and Bina already had light of Hassadim in abundance, Ima’s posterior was then annulled. For she preferred the light of Hassadim to the light of Hochma only when she lacked Hassadim, but after she already had Hassadim in abundance, she turned herself back toward the light of Hochma and annulled her posterior. Then the screen that relies on her posterior was also refined, for its detaining force weakened. However, it was not refined all at once, but only in the order of the degree, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 199:3
items.html: (to question) At first there was Lo Mati in Keter and Mati in HB, and illumination of GAR returned to the Partzuf. This illumination was through turning of the face and not through refinement. Afterwards, ZON of Keter were refined from phase three and phase two to phase two and phase one, and the light of Hesed was given to the vessel of Hochma, and from there to the vessels of VAK. The anterior vessels—Hesed, Tifferet, Hod and Malchut—shone, meaning according to the order of Mati and Lo Mati, as it was in Partzuf AB, until the light reached Malchut. Then the screen was refined, all light ceased from the Partzuf, and the screen, incorporated with all the records, rose to the vessel of Keter. Then Bina again felt the lack of Hassadim and therefore turned her posterior back toward Hochma. The screen of phase two then returned to its original strength and again drew the level of phase two to Keter. The light of Hassadim again returned to fill the Partzuf abundantly, and then Bina again annulled her posterior and the screen weakened once more. Thus, it repeats cyclically and continually. (page 344, the passage beginning “And the reason”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 200:1
items.html: (to question) In truth, there is only the vessel of Malchut here, and the restriction and the screen do not rest on any discernment of the first nine at all. The entire matter of the screen rising to the first discernments was only by the force of the ascent and refinement of the discernment of Malchut, which equalized with them in her measure of coarseness. Therefore, when the screen rose to Bina, it means that it received the discernment of the posterior of Bina as its detaining discernment over Malchut that rose there. However, afterwards, in the Partzufim below this Partzuf SAG, the discernment of Malchut had already mingled in the self of the first nine Sefirot so that the discernment of the restriction itself rests upon them. Then the screen does not rely on the posterior of Bina; rather, the force of the restriction itself rests upon it, even in the screen of phase one.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 201:1
items.html: (to question) You see in the order of the cascading of the Partzufim that the light of Keter of the upper Partzuf remains concealed in the Rosh and does not return to the lower Partzuf. The light of Keter of Partzuf Keter of AK did not return to Partzuf AB of AK, and Keter of Partzuf AB received from it only the discernment of VAK. Likewise, Keter of Partzuf AB remained concealed and did not return to Partzuf SAG of AK, and Keter of Partzuf SAG receives from it only VAK. It is likewise in all the Partzufim. It is known that the essence of the Partzuf is discerned only by the name of the upper Sefira. Since the lower Partzuf has only VAK of the upper Sefira, it is therefore regarded in its entirety as VAK relative to the upper one. You also know that these GAR of the upper Sefira, which the lower one lacks, remain standing in the Rosh under Malchut of the Rosh. The light of Keter lacking in Partzuf AB remained there under Malchut of the Rosh, and likewise the light of Keter of AB that did not return to Partzuf SAG remained standing under Malchut of the Rosh. Thus, the entire difference between the Rosh and the Guf is only in GAR, for VAK reach the Guf through Keter of the Guf, which receives VAK from the light of Keter that remains in the Rosh. Therefore, we call every Rosh by the name GAR, and every Guf by the name VAK or ZAT, since this is the full measure of the difference between them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:1
items.html: It was already explained above in answer 201 that every lower one lacks GAR of the upper Sefira of the upper one, and is therefore regarded as VAK of the upper one, since the essence of the Partzuf is its upper Sefira. All this is relative to the upper one, but relative to itself it has all ten Sefirot. For example, Partzuf AB has illumination of VAK of Keter of Partzuf Keter and is therefore regarded relative to it as VAK. However, relative to itself, its upper Sefira is Hochma and not Keter, and it has GAR of Hochma in completeness. Likewise, Partzuf Bina has VAK of the upper Sefira of Partzuf AB, which is Hochma, but of its own upper Sefira it has GAR in completeness, and likewise with all of them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:2
items.html: Additional explanation of the matter of turning of the face and the order of the formation of vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:3
items.html: What is brought here from item 15 through item 20 in the words of the ARI. Although the matters are sufficiently revealed in Inner Light in their place there, nevertheless, I saw that the students become confused and find it difficult to arrange the matters so as to understand the words of the ARI there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:4
items.html: Here we must remember separately the matter of the departure of the light, the matter of the refinement of the screen, and the matter of the turning of the face of the vessels. With all of them, we must remember the form of each and every vessel in itself.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:5
items.html: The formation of the vessels occurs only after the departure of the last light from the vessel, as the ARI says in item 27. And these are his words: “Know that all these vessels did not become coarse and become vessels until after the departure of the light of Malchut, at which time it turns its face away from the vessel,” and so forth; study it there well. Thus, the matter of the turning of the face of the vessels begins in each and every vessel from the time the light of Malchut departs from it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:6
items.html: You already know the quality of the vessels: Each one must contain the discernment of coarseness corresponding to the level of its light. The vessel is called only by the name of the upper Sefira on its level. If the upper Sefira is Hochma, even though all the Sefirot below Hochma are necessarily there, it is nevertheless called only a vessel of Hochma. Likewise, if the upper Sefira is Keter, it is called only a vessel of Keter, and so forth in this manner. You also know the measure of coarseness in each vessel required for the measure of its level. The vessel of Keter, in which there is the level of Yechida, must have coarseness of phase four in the vessel. If the screen that rests upon the coarseness of phase four in the vessel is refined, all the light of Keter immediately disappears from there. It is only the light of Yechida, but it contains all the lights below this light, as explained above. Needless to say, if the vessel itself lacked coarseness of phase four, it would then be entirely unfit to receive the screen of phase four, and it would certainly not be a vessel of Keter at all, which is evaluated only according to the coarseness within it. The same applies to all the vessels. This is simple, for after the discernment of coarseness exists in the vessel itself, the screen can be discussed. But if the vessel itself is deficient, the screen cannot complement it at all, for a screen means a detaining discernment that rests upon a known measure of the coarseness of the vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:7
items.html: You also know that the matter of coarseness in the vessel and the matter of the clothing of the light are two opposites. For example, the vessel of Malchut, which has coarseness of phase four, is nevertheless unfit because of this to clothe the level of Yechida, for it lacks the discernment of clothing of that level, which is the vessel of Keter. It follows that the distinction between the vessel of Keter and the vessel of Malchut is this: The vessel of Keter has phase four of drawing and also the discernment of Keter of clothing. But the vessel of Malchut has only phase four of drawing, while it lacks phase four of clothing, meaning the discernment of the vessel of Keter. Likewise, the distinction between the vessel of Hochma and the vessel of ZA is that the vessel of Hochma has phase three of drawing and also the vessel of Hochma, which is phase three of clothing. But the vessel of ZA has only phase three of drawing, and from the discernment of clothing it has only the vessel of ZA, which is fit to clothe only the level of Ruach, the level of phase one. It lacks phase three of clothing, and the same applies to all of them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:8
items.html: With this you will understand that when the light departed from Malchut because the screen of phase four was refined, at which time Malchut rose to ZA, in truth only the light of Yechida departed from the Partzuf, from the vessel of Keter, since it now lacked the discernment of drawing. But the light of Malchut did not depart at all, for it rose to the vessel of ZA. Nevertheless, by this only the vessel of Malchut was made, and not the vessel of Keter. This is because the vessel of Malchut remained entirely without light, whereas the vessel of Keter still had light. Although it was the light of Hochma, far lower than its own discernment, this is nevertheless not regarded as sufficient departure for it to turn its face downward and become a vessel. That occurred only after even the light of Malchut departed from the vessel of Keter, as explained above in the words of the ARI. Therefore, only Malchut became a vessel, since she was entirely without light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:9
items.html: Likewise, for example, when the light of Malchut departed from ZA and rose to Bina, the vessel of ZA then turned its face downward, even though the light of ZA had not yet departed, for it rose to Bina. Rather, the light of Hochma now departed from the vessel of Hochma. Nevertheless, Hochma did not become a vessel; only ZA became a vessel, because only ZA now remained without light, whereas in the vessel of Hochma there was still the light of Bina, and so forth in this manner.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:10
items.html: Therefore, after all the lights departed from the Partzuf, all the vessels remained with the face of the lower one at the posterior of the upper one, except for the vessels of Keter and Hochma, which remained face to face. For then all the vessels turned their faces back as in the beginning. It follows that the face of the vessel of Malchut, which is phase four, is opposite the posterior of the vessel of ZA, which is phase two. Likewise, the face of the vessel of ZA, which is phase three, is opposite the posterior of the vessel of Bina, which is phase one. Likewise, the face of Bina, which is phase two, is opposite the posterior of Hochma, which is also phase two. But Keter remained with its face downward because it could not turn its face back as in the beginning, since the record of phase four had disappeared, as is known. Therefore, it remained in phase three downward opposite Hochma, whose face is also phase three, and Keter and Hochma were face to face.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section V, List of Answers on Topics 202:11
items.html: (to question) We must also understand that the measures of the level extended according to the coarseness in the screen are evaluated by the measure of clothing of the Sefirot of direct light. For example, when we say the level of phase one, the intention is the measure of light that phase three of direct light, called ZA, can receive within it, which is two lights, Ruach and Nefesh. When we say the level of phase two, this is according to the measure of clothing in phase two of direct light. The level of Hochma is according to the measure of clothing of Hochma of direct light, and so forth in this manner.
